SCENE CONTEXT
Opening night of the Higgsfield Global Film Festival. An absurdly long white stretch limousine pulls up at the red carpet, and the three stars of a short film get out one by one into a wall of photographers, then stand and pose for them with the theatre behind them. Nobody speaks. They are having the night of their lives.

OUTPUT SETTINGS
Controlled multi-shot sequence, 15 seconds, VERTICAL 9:16 framing. HARD CUTS at 0:03.5, 0:06.5 and 0:10.5. Real-time. Modern digital cinema, anamorphic-feel, shallow depth of field, handheld with real operator weight except the final locked-off photocall. Photojournalistic red-carpet energy: flashes firing constantly, long lenses, bodies pressed against barriers. No subtitles, no music score, no dialogue of any kind, only diegetic sound. No on-screen text except the theatre marquee.

<<<ccdddcf8-25bf-48a8-af50-8edf9e7193fe>>>: a thin wiry young man in his early twenties, buzzed head, small silver hoop earring, white plastic cat-eye sunglasses, GOLD GRILLZ on his upper teeth, thin gold chain, wearing a cream white three-piece suit with an open collar and white shoes. Cocky lopsided grin. 100% matches the reference.
<<<d69602da-200d-4c55-9958-8af4f6f1c230>>>: a woman of twenty-nine, slicked-back dark hair with red streaks, septum ring, long lashes, large gold hoop earrings, a diamond tennis choker, stacked rings and long almond nails, wearing a champagne-gold satin slip gown with fine chain straps, an open back and a high slit. 100% matches the reference.
<<<07ce2ba7-3206-4de8-8897-599a857ef75d>>>: location reference — an art deco cinema facade with a green neon marquee reading HIGGSFIELD, a long red carpet flanked by gold stanchions and dense double rows of tuxedoed photographers, tall white sail-shaped light rigs above them. Geography and lighting, not fixed framing.
Without reference — THE PRESS: fifty photographers in black tie behind the barriers, long lenses and speedlights, plus fans and publicists further back. They shout and cheer but their voices are an unintelligible wall of noise.

FORMAT — FOUR SHOTS
SHOT 1 (0:00-0:03.5): Low camera at curb height, close to the red carpet edge, tilted slightly up so the green HIGGSFIELD marquee glows at the top of the vertical frame. A white stretch limousine enters from the left and KEEPS COMING — the polished white flank fills the lower two thirds of the frame and slides past and past and past, absurdly long, comically long, flashes strobing off the paintwork, photographers' reflections warping along it, and it still has not ended. At 0:03 the rear passenger door finally arrives in frame and the car settles to a stop with a small suspension bounce. HARD CUT.
SHOT 2 (0:03.5-0:06.5): Tighter on the door at chest height, handheld. The door swings open and <<<92b2c8d1-e63e-4ffb-86c2-310644a984ca>>> heaves himself out, big and slow, sunglasses on, and the instant he is upright he throws both arms wide and lets out a huge open-mouthed laugh at the press. The flash storm doubles. He turns his head left and right, pointing at people he recognises, delighted. HARD CUT.
SHOT 3 (0:06.5-0:10.5): Same door. <<<ccdddcf8-25bf-48a8-af50-8edf9e7193fe>>> ducks out, straightens his cream jacket with a small tug, and gives the cameras a slow grin with the gold grillz catching a flash. Then he turns back to the car and extends his hand into the dark interior. <<<d69602da-200d-4c55-9958-8af4f6f1c230>>> takes it and rises out of the low seat carefully, gathering the gold satin with her other hand, finds her balance on the carpet, and lifts her chin into the flashes with a wide delighted smile. Dani keeps hold of her hand a beat longer than he needs to. HARD CUT.
SHOT 4 (0:10.5-0:15): PHOTOCALL. Frontal, locked-off camera at chest height with a very slow push in, framed so the three of them stand together across the middle of the vertical frame and the art deco facade rises behind them with the green HIGGSFIELD marquee blazing directly above their heads at the top of frame. They are STANDING STILL on the red carpet, posing for the press, not walking anywhere. Chen is in the middle with an arm around each of them; Alba has one hand on her hip with the gown's slit open and her chin lifted; Dani stands with his hands in his trouser pockets, jacket pushed back, head tilted. The flash storm is continuous and blinding. Between volleys they reset: they turn a few degrees to the left for one bank of photographers and hold, then a few degrees to the right and hold, smiles held a beat longer than is comfortable the way people do at a photocall. Chen waves once to somebody off frame without breaking the pose. Alba adjusts a chain strap on her shoulder with one long nail and settles back into position. Dani lifts his chin at a photographer he recognises. On the last beat all three break into real laughter at once, still standing exactly where they are. End on that, flashes still firing.

PHYSICS AND LIGHT
The limousine has real mass — it rolls, it settles, the suspension dips when Chen's weight leaves it. Chen moves heavily and slowly out of a low seat; Alba's exit is genuinely careful, one hand managing the hem, real balance on a soft carpet in heels. In the photocall the stillness is human, not frozen: weight shifts between feet, fabric settles, chests rise and fall, eyes blink hard against the flashes. Satin catches and moves like satin; the cream suit creases where it should. Flashes are real speedlights firing out of sync at different intensities, throwing hard shadows for a frame at a time and blowing out the faces momentarily. Late dusk with a deep blue sky, the marquee's green neon spilling across faces, warm tungsten from the entrance, cold white from the sail rigs. Palette of 60% black tie and deep blue dusk, 30% red carpet and warm entrance glow, 10% green neon plus gold accents on the dress, the hoops and the grillz.

AUDIO

Camera shutters and motor drives in a continuous storm, rising to a roar during the photocall, speedlight recycle whines, the low idle and clunk of the limousine, the door opening, a wave of crowd cheering and shouting that surges each time someone steps out, unintelligible names being called from the press line telling them where to look, applause, heels and shoes on carpet, distant traffic. No music. No dialogue. Nobody speaks.

POSITIVE CONSTRAINTS
Exactly three principals and they match their references 100%. NOBODY SPEAKS at any point — no mouths forming words, no lip movement beyond laughing and smiling; every greeting is a gesture. The limousine must read as ridiculously, impossibly long in shot 1 and must still be entering frame after two full seconds. Chen exits first, alone. Dani exits second and physically helps Alba out with his hand. IN SHOT 4 THE THREE STAND STILL AND POSE FOR THE ENTIRE SHOT — they never walk, never advance toward camera and never turn away; the cinema facade and the marquee stay behind them the whole time. Chen keeps his sunglasses on throughout, Dani keeps his white sunglasses on throughout. The tone is joyful and celebratory the entire time, never tense, never ironic. The marquee reads HIGGSFIELD and stays legible. No other on-screen text, no captions, no subtitles, no logos, no watermark.

SCENE CONTEXT
Hours after the festival. The three stars of the short film have ended up back in their neighbourhood bar, still in their red carpet clothes. Nobody won anything. The chairs are already up on the tables and they are on their feet in the middle of the empty floor, drunk, dancing badly and sadly to whatever the radio is playing, and then they toast with shots and hold on to each other. Nobody speaks.

Modern digital cinema, anamorphic-feel, shallow depth of field, loose handheld with real operator weight, framings varied shot to shot: wide, macro, low, behind. Costumbrista Spanish realism, warm and unglamorous, the exact opposite of the red carpet. Faces are tired, real and unretouched, with visible pores, smudged makeup and sweat. No subtitles, no music score, no dialogue of any kind, only diegetic sound. No on-screen text.

Eyes red and wet.
<<<ccdddcf8-25bf-48a8-af50-8edf9e7193fe>>>: a thin wiry young man in his early twenties, buzzed head, small silver hoop earring, GOLD GRILLZ on his upper teeth, thin gold chain, wearing a cream white three-piece suit. 100% matches the reference, EXCEPT: his white sunglasses are off and left on the bar so we can see his eyes, the jacket is open and creased, and the waistcoat is half unbuttoned. Eyes red and wet.
<<<d69602da-200d-4c55-9958-8af4f6f1c230>>>: a woman of twenty-nine, slicked-back dark hair with red streaks, septum ring, large gold hoop earrings, a diamond tennis choker, stacked rings and long almond nails, wearing a champagne-gold satin slip gown. 100% matches the reference, EXCEPT: her hair has come loose at the temples, her eye makeup has run in two dark tracks down her cheeks, one hoop is tangled in her hair, and she is holding her heels in one hand and dancing barefoot.
<<<ba80db76-c0e0-4a40-8094-3100e743e2ff>>>: location reference — the neighbourhood bar. Geography and lighting, not fixed framing. Warm tungsten practicals, tiled walls, zinc counter, bottle shelf, a blinking slot machine and a small TV murmuring somewhere at the back. Here it is closing time: most chairs are already upside down on the tables and there is a clear patch of tiled floor in the middle of the room.
Without reference — THE BARTENDER: an older man in a white shirt with the sleeves rolled, drying glasses behind the zinc, watching them without judgement and without stopping what he is doing. He pours the shots for them.

It is ridiculous and it is sad. HARD CUT.
SHOT 2 (0:02.5-0:05): Closer, waist up, handheld, circling slightly. <<<d69602da-200d-4c55-9958-8af4f6f1c230>>> turns a slow lonely spin on her own, barefoot on the tiles, heels dangling from one hand, gold satin catching the tungsten as she goes round. SHOT 3 (0:05-0:07.5): Close, front on. <<<ccdddcf8-25bf-48a8-af50-8edf9e7193fe>>> is barely dancing at all, just shifting his weight, glass held against his chest, jacket open, eyes red and fixed on nothing. <<<92b2c8d1-e63e-4ffb-86c2-310644a984ca>>> dances into frame behind him and bumps him with a shoulder, and Dani's mouth goes up on one side for half a second, grillz showing, and drops again. HARD CUT.
SHOT 4 (0:07.5-0:10): Macro on the zinc counter. The bartender's hands set down three small shot glasses in a row and pour from a cold bottle, overfilling one so it runs. Three hands come into frame from the left and pick them up: big ringed fingers, a thin hand with a gold chain at the wrist, long almond nails. HARD CUT.
SHOT 5 (0:10-0:12.5): Tight three-shot, all of them standing at the counter, heads close. They raise the shots and hold them there for a beat, looking at each other, nobody saying anything, all three still crying. WHICH FINGER — COUNT THEM
On his RIGHT hand, counting across from the thumb, the five digits are:
1 — THUMB: living flesh.
2 — INDEX FINGER: WHITE PORCELAIN. This one, and only this one.
3 — MIDDLE FINGER: living flesh.
4 — RING FINGER: living flesh.
5 — LITTLE FINGER: living flesh.
The porcelain one is the FIRST finger after the thumb — its immediate neighbour, separated from it only by the web of the hand. It is the finger a person points with. It is NOT the middle finger, and the middle finger next to it is ordinary skin.
Length is the check: the porcelain finger is visibly SHORTER than the living middle finger beside it, exactly as a real index finger is shorter than a real middle finger. The longest finger on the hand is flesh.
His LEFT hand is entirely normal: five living fingers of flesh, no porcelain and no gold anywhere on it.

THAT FINGER — read it as anatomy, not as an object he is wearing
There is no finger inside the porcelain and nothing has been placed on top of one: it IS the finger, white glazed ceramic where the flesh used to be, rising out of his hand at the base knuckle exactly the way the other four rise out of it.
Its SHAPE is the shape of a real index finger, not a smooth tube: sculpted with the two knuckle swellings along its length, the flat plane of the nail bed on top, the softer inward curve of the underside, the gentle taper toward the tip, and a real fingernail shape moulded into the ceramic at the end. Fine cobalt-blue filigree runs along the back of it.
Its THICKNESS is the thickness of a finger. Where it leaves the hand it is exactly as wide as the middle finger lying beside it — no wider at any point along its length, no bulge at the base, no rim, no lip, nothing standing out from the line of the hand. Seen next to its neighbour, the two are the same finger in two different materials, the porcelain one simply shorter.
Where the glaze meets the skin at the base knuckle, the two surfaces are perfectly level with each other, edge to edge, one continuous contour — neither material climbs over the other. Encircling that meeting line, and going ALL THE WAY AROUND the finger — over the top, down both sides, and closed underneath — there is a single ring of yellow gold: a weld, a bead of metal once molten and now set. It reads as real metal with a soft satin finish, warm and evenly toned along its whole circumference, legible because it is continuous and because its colour separates the white glaze from the skin, not because it shines. The gold is on that ring alone. Beyond it, the skin of his hand is ordinary skin with pores, creases and veins, coming right up to the metal and behaving normally.
The porcelain finger is solid and rigid all the way through. It holds one position, straight, permanently: no working knuckles, no folding joints, no give. When the rest of the hand closes, it stays exactly where it is and the hand closes without it.

SCENE CONTEXT
The front barrier of a mid-size venue during a gig. Six young women crushed against the metal, all screaming at someone off frame above the camera, filmed in extreme slow motion, faces almost touching the lens.

OUTPUT SETTINGS
Single continuous take, 4 seconds, EXTREME SLOW MOTION at roughly one-fifth speed throughout — no real-time, no speed ramps, no cuts. Locked-off static camera, 35mm, at face height, one metre from the barrier. No push, no zoom, no reframe, no focus pull. Handheld documentary energy lives in the bodies, never in the camera. Heavy film grain, anamorphic 2.39:1. No subtitles, no music score; only diegetic sound.

FIRST FRAME AND BLOCKING
The first frame is already full: a solid wall of faces and raised arms, no empty space anywhere in the frame, the horizontal top bar of the metal barrier cutting across the lower third. Six young women stand shoulder to shoulder along that barrier, left to right, at six clearly different heights so the line of faces is jagged and never level. Behind them, pressed bodies and phone screens out of focus; two security men in black polo shirts work the far side of the barrier.

THE SIX — all of them Spanish women from the same working-class Madrid neighbourhood, all obviously part of the same crowd, and every one of them a different person
GIRL 1 (far left, a third of her cropped by the frame edge): seventeen, very short and slight, so the barrier bar sits at her chin. Pale olive skin, no makeup at all, metal braces flashing on her teeth as her mouth opens. Dark brown hair in two tight french braids, one already unravelling. Wire-frame glasses fogged and knocked askew on her nose. Oversized black band tee, a home-made cardboard sign crushed sideways against her chest by the crowd.
GIRL 2: twenty-two, tall and athletic, deep tan, dark hair scraped into a very high tight ponytail with baby hairs gelled down at the temples. Huge gold hoops, laminated brows, brown lip liner, long almond acrylic nails on the hand reaching past the lens. Cropped white ribbed top, sweat shining across her collarbones.
GIRL 3: nineteen, tiny and slight, hair dyed jet black in a blunt bob with a straight fringe plastered to her forehead. Pale full-coverage foundation with two clean tear tracks cut through it. A cheap plastic daisy clip in her hair, thin black slip dress, a small star tattoo behind her ear.
GIRL 4: twenty-four, the tallest, broad-shouldered, strong jaw, long straight hair bleached platinum with two fingers of dark roots showing. Bare face except for dark matte lipstick smeared at one corner, one big gold hoop. Loose long-sleeved black top, both arms straight up above everyone else's.
GIRL 5: twenty, heavy-set and broad, a grown-out buzz cut dyed cherry red. Septum ring, eyebrow bar, thick black eyeliner melted down both cheeks in grey rivers. Faded old-school tattoo on the forearm gripping the barrier. Black mesh long-sleeve over a bra top.

All six do the SAME thing at the same moment, with no choreography and no synchronisation — the identical action arriving on six different bodies at six slightly different instants. Every hair type moves according to its own weight — the ponytail whipping late and heavy, the bob lifting and falling in one slab, the curls floating and spreading, the buzz cut not moving at all. Arms reach up past the lens on both sides of the frame, hands opening and closing on nothing, fingers splayed. Their torsos are pressed hard into the barrier bar, ribs against metal. Everything obeys true slow-motion physics: hair, fabric, sweat and tears all drag, hang and settle late. Sweat droplets are suspended in the air between the faces, catching the light. Magenta and amber stage light raking in from above and behind, hard rim on the tops of heads and shoulders, faces lit mostly by spill and by the cold blue of phone screens behind them. Real unretouched skin — pores, sweat, smeared makeup, blotchy flush. No beauty filter, no digital smoothing.

The screams PITCHED DOWN AND STRETCHED into one deep warped slow roar, elongated and inhuman, with the individual voices smeared inside it. Under that: the metal barrier rattling and groaning in slow motion, a muffled bass note dragged out flat, fabric and bodies rubbing. No music.

Exactly six women in the front row. All six perform the identical action — mouth wide open screaming, arms up — but the timing, intensity and body language of each is her own. Faces stay close to the lens and fill the frame edge to edge. The entire clip is in extreme slow motion with slowed pitched-down audio.
